items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Real giants, I had always looked up to that band and Carney, Cootie, everybody.

ctx.x: Cat Anderson was in the band, and Julian Priestley and I went down just before we went to work, we went down to Masie Hall where they were getting it together, you know, Joe Benjamin. Duke Ellington's valet, a friend of mine, he said, "Man, I want you to meet Duke." I said, "Well, I met Duke before," which I had out in Chicago, back in the '60s. Paul and I were hanging out one night at E. Parker McDougall (PHONETIC) and Paul Gonzalves say, "Man, you probably bring

Wilbur down to the studio," -- we recording down there tomorrow -- he says, "I want Duke to hear him." (Unintelligible) John Lamb was playing bass with him and they were talking about trying to get me in the band. Well, I was crazy to (unintelligible) accept a gig because I had too much respect for Duke, you know, to get in the band and know he'd be writing music and all that and I couldn't read it.
